text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's Association of Commercial Bank (ACB) holds an annual meeting today expected to approve the 1996 annual report and amendments to the statutes and elect a new co-chairman.

-- Natural gas deliveries by Russia's gas giant Gazprom to Bulgaria for the next 15 years were guaranteed at prices below the current ones, Vassil Filipov, executive director of Bulgaria's gas company Bulgargas, said after a visit to Moscow. @

-- Incomes of Bulgarians are expected to rise two-fold by the year's end from the current levels, Valentin Vassilev from the main anti-communist United Democratic Forces favoured to win the upcoming elections on April 19, said during a election debate.

-- Some 30 percent of Bulgarians are now backing wider powers for the country's president and a change from a parliamentary into a presidential republic mainly due to the personality and the actions of incumbent President Petar Stoyanov, a survey by Market Test polling agency showed. @
-- The planned sale of a stake in the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company could be expected at the end of this year at the earliest, cabinet's advisor on concessions Todor Popov said.

-- The new Euro-Left political formation which includes mainly former Socialist dissidents, will back urgent economic reforms proposed by the main anti-communist United Democratic Forces in the new parliament to asemble after general elections in April, an Euro-Left leader said. @
-- Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation for March was expected at 10 percent at most, a National Statistics Institute forecast showed.
-- Bulgaria's Central Co-operative Bank decided to raise capital to 15 billion levs from four billion levs, the bank's management said.
Ex-finance minister in the former Socialist cabinet Dimitar Kostov and Momchil Andreev, former head of state-owned Post Bank, were elected as deputy board chairmen.

-- Caretaker Interior minister Bogomil Bonev is likely to retain his post in a possible future cabinet of the United Democratic Forces (UDF) due to decisive steps he had taken to crack down on crime in the country, UDF leader Ivan Kostov said.
Latest opinion polls showed the UDF a favourite to win the April general election.
